Why this usually goes wrong

Paper loses everything the week the person keeping it goes on leave. Big foreign software keeps everything, and nobody on the floor opens it. We built around both.

Nobody needs an account

The QR code on the machine opens a short form. No login, no password, nothing to set up. So problems get reported when someone sees them, not at the end of the shift.

It comes out of your running costs

One price for the whole company, in dirhams, from 1 000 MAD a month. Small enough that you sign it off yourself.

We do the setting up

No servers to buy, no six-month project. Send us the files you already keep. We move everything across, set up your machines, and you're running in a week.

The numbers write themselves

You don't fill anything in. Closing jobs does it.

Your figures stay current

Uptime, MTBF, MTTR, how long machines sat idle. All of it moves as jobs get closed, so there's no monthly report to put together.

Servicing schedules itself

Tell it a compressor needs looking at every 4 000 hours and it writes that job itself, a few days ahead, every time.

Nothing gets lost

Every approval, every change, every closed job keeps the name and the time it happened.

Things a foreign supplier can't offer

Not because their software is worse. Because they aren't here.

Your data stays in Morocco

Not on a server in a country you'd struggle to point to on a map.

You pay in dirhams

The same amount every month. No exchange rate, and no extra charge each time you take someone on.

We can come to the plant

Same time zone, French or English, and someone who can stand in front of the machine with you.

Made in Morocco

Local industry, local tools. There are very few of us doing this here.

Our first twenty factories

We're looking for twenty plants to run this properly. Send us whatever you keep today — your spreadsheets, your machine list — and we'll do the rest: set it up, print your QR codes, train your team on site.

You'll be up and running before you've had to work anything out. All we ask in return is that you tell us honestly how it goes.
